context_prefix_rationale: TSK_FCSD_* is consumed by SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_NC_v1 (25 tasks). Using FCRP_ (FiberCement RePaint) eliminates all ID collisions. Verified: TSK_FCRP_* has zero existing usage in the codebase. Pattern follows established convention: FC = fiber cement, RP = repaint.
scope_summary: Combined condition assessment + prep + prime + finish repaint spec for previously painted exterior fiber cement siding (James Hardie HardiePlank, HardieShingle, HardiePanel, and equivalents). Covers assessment (condition rating, adhesion test, chalk test, moisture probe, mildew/algae scan, caulk assessment), gentle cleaning (low-pressure rinse — NO power washing), condition-driven prep (scrape/feather failing areas, chalk remediation, degloss/scuff, mildew treatment), caulk assessment and replacement (significant scope — every butt joint, corner, window/door perimeter), state-driven primer (chalk-binding, spot acrylic, full acrylic, or alkali-resistant on exposed bare FC), finish coat application (spray primary — NO back-rolling on FC), interstage protocol, final walkthrough, landscape/hardscape protection, and RRP containment for pre-1978. Uses SF as primary UOM with siding profile modifier (lap/panel/shingle) and surface texture modifier (smooth/cedarmill/roughsawn). Access type drives height modifier per elevation. QT2-QT4 (QT5 excluded per Exterior_Substrates_Doctrine §5.4 — siding is utilitarian surface). Sheens: flat, satin (NOT semi-gloss or gloss). 4 exterior RP substrate states. Condition scale GOOD/FAIR/POOR drives prep intensity. Lead-safe RRP gate for pre-1978. spray_backroll is the primary RP application method (departure from NC spray-only — existing painted FC benefits from backroll for adhesion into surface imperfections unlike factory-smooth NC). brush_roll is fallback. Single mobilization: assess + prep + prime + finish.

relevant_findings.topic: Fiber cement RP differs from NC in application method: spray_backroll replaces spray-only
relevant_findings.finding: NC fiber cement siding is spray-only — NO back-rolling because the factory-smooth surface produces stipple/orange peel with backroll. However, RP fiber cement has an existing paint film with weathering, micro-cracking, surface texture from previous coats, and repaired areas. The surface is no longer factory-smooth. Spray_backroll is the correct primary method for RP fiber cement: spray for coverage speed, backroll to work product into surface irregularities for maximum adhesion on the weathered existing film. This aligns with the wood siding RP pattern (SF_SIDING_WOOD_EXT_RP_v1 uses spray_backbrush). brush_roll is fallback for small areas (<750 SF), occupied-adjacent, or high wind.
relevant_findings.source: Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine; SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_NC_v1/spec.json KD-003 (NC spray-only rationale); SF_SIDING_WOOD_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json (spray_backbrush for wood RP)

relevant_findings.topic: NO power washing on fiber cement — even for repaint prep
relevant_findings.finding: High-pressure power washing is PROHIBITED on fiber cement in ALL contexts including repaint. Even at moderate pressure (1500-2000 PSI), power washing strips existing paint films, damages embossed texture profiles (cedarmill, roughsawn), and forces water behind the wall assembly through butt joints and J-channels. Fiber cement RP cleaning uses LOW-PRESSURE RINSE ONLY: garden hose with soft-bristle brush, or gentle power rinse at 400-600 PSI maximum with wide fan tip (40-60 degree). TSP solution for stubborn dirt/chalk at QT3+. This is a CRITICAL departure from wood siding RP (which uses 1000-1500 PSI power wash) and exterior trim RP (which uses 500-1000 PSI). Allow 24-48 hr dry time after rinse before coating.

relevant_findings.topic: Four exterior RP substrate states apply to fiber cement siding
relevant_findings.finding: Exterior RP uses 4 substrate states from controlled_enums.json: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (adhered, minimal chalk — degloss/scuff only, common on well-maintained FC), SS_EXT_CHALKING (surface chalk present — chalk remediation + chalk-binding primer, common on south/west elevations after 8-12 years), SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (cracking/alligatoring — scrape/feather + spot or full prime, often at butt joints and caulk failure points), SS_EXT_PEELING (active coating lifting — heavy scrape/feather + full prime + alkali-resistant primer on exposed bare FC at pH 13.0, most labor-intensive state). SS_EXT_WEATHERED is excluded — weathered bare FC with no coating is NC territory requiring full re-prime. SS_EXT_STAINED_* states are excluded — stained FC is not standard scope. Per-elevation substrate state if conditions differ across building faces.
relevant_findings.source: controlled_enums.json substrate_state; SF_SIDING_WOOD_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json (4-state exterior siding RP pattern); SF_TRIM_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json (4-state exterior RP pattern)

relevant_findings.topic: Exposed bare fiber cement in RP context requires alkali-resistant primer
relevant_findings.finding: When paint fails on fiber cement siding and scraping exposes bare substrate, the cementitious matrix is at pH 13.0 — identical to NC bare FC. Alkali-resistant primer (SW Loxon Masonry Primer or equivalent) is MANDATORY on any exposed bare FC areas to prevent saponification (alkaline burn) of latex binders. This is a critical RP-specific primer path that does not exist in wood siding RP. In NC, alkali-resistant primer is needed for SS_EXT_BARE_FIBERCEMENT. In RP, it is triggered when SS_EXT_PEELING or SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT scraping exposes bare substrate. The primer chemistry is substrate-driven (what is exposed), not condition-driven (how bad it is).

relevant_findings.topic: Chalking is extremely common on fiber cement siding — primary RP degradation mode
relevant_findings.finding: Chalking (gradual UV degradation of paint binder leaving powdery residue) is the most common degradation mode for painted fiber cement siding. FC's dense, non-porous surface causes paint film to age differently than on wood — instead of cracking from substrate movement (wood), FC paint primarily degrades via UV binder breakdown (chalking). South and west elevations chalk faster (direct UV). Chalk layer prevents topcoat adhesion even though the surface appears intact. Treatment: low-pressure rinse to remove loose chalk, chalk rub test after rinse, chalk-binding primer if moderate/heavy chalk remains. Chalk-binding primer penetrates and binds residual chalk layer. This is the single most common RP scenario for fiber cement — many FC repaint jobs are chalking-only with no mechanical failure.

relevant_findings.topic: Caulk assessment and replacement is MAJOR scope on fiber cement siding RP
relevant_findings.finding: Fiber cement siding has significantly more caulked joints than wood siding: every siding-to-trim junction (corner boards, window casings, door casings, frieze), every butt joint on lap siding (where adjacent boards meet mid-run), and siding-to-foundation transitions. NC caulks siding-to-trim joints only — field butt joints are NOT caulked per NC spec (moisture trap risk). RP caulk assessment uses the 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol: trace every joint where water could enter, assess condition (intact/cracked/failed), remove failed caulk, re-caulk with exterior-grade paintable caulk (polyurethane or siliconized acrylic). Caulk failure on FC is a major moisture intrusion pathway — water enters behind siding at failed joints, causing substrate damage and accelerating paint failure. RP DOES assess butt joint caulk (even though NC doesn't apply it) because previous painters or installers may have caulked them, and failed butt joint caulk is an active water intrusion point.
relevant_findings.source: Exterior_Caulking_Sealants_Doctrine ('Think Like a Water Drop'); SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_NC_v1/spec.json (NC caulk scope); SF_SIDING_WOOD_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json (RP caulk assessment pattern)

relevant_findings.topic: ColorPlus / factory-finished FC in RP context — bonding primer on exposed factory finish
relevant_findings.finding: Previously painted ColorPlus/ExpertFinish fiber cement (factory-finished, then field-painted during NC) presents a unique RP substrate: when RP paint fails and scraping exposes the original factory-finished surface underneath the field paint, the exposed oven-baked factory finish requires bonding primer — same as NC SS_EXT_FACTORY_FINISHED. This is a secondary primer path that applies only when the underlying substrate is factory-finished FC rather than standard factory-primed FC. During RP assessment, the estimator should note if the original substrate is ColorPlus/ExpertFinish (visible at exposed areas by the characteristic multi-coat factory finish color). Most RP fiber cement will be standard factory-primed-then-painted, not ColorPlus.
relevant_findings.source: SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_NC_v1/spec.json RC-001 (ColorPlus inclusion); SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_NC_v1/research.json RF-010 (ColorPlus in NC scope)

relevant_findings.topic: Siding profile and surface texture modifiers transfer unchanged from NC to RP
relevant_findings.finding: Siding profile (lap/panel/shingle) and surface texture (smooth/cedarmill/roughsawn) are physical characteristics that do not change between NC and RP. Production rate modifiers transfer directly: profile modifier (lap=1.00, panel=1.10, shingle=2.00) and texture modifier (smooth=1.00, cedarmill=1.20, roughsawn=1.30). These apply to both prep and coating tasks in RP. Shingle siding remains dramatically slower in RP — complex geometry slows scraping, priming, and coating equally. Maximum modifier stacking: shingle (2.00) x roughsawn (1.30) x scaffold (1.60) = 4.16x — exceeds 4.0x cap, recommend hourly billing for this combination (same as NC finding).

relevant_findings.topic: Condition assessment is mandatory before fiber cement RP work
relevant_findings.finding: Fiber cement siding RP requires multi-point assessment before prep or coating. Assessment tasks: (1) Visual condition inspection — scan all siding field surfaces per elevation for chalking, cracking, peeling, adhesion failure, mildew/algae, efflorescence, joint failure; photograph defects; assign substrate state. (2) Adhesion test — ASTM D3359 cross-hatch tape test on representative sections per elevation; critical on chalking surfaces where adhesion may appear sound but chalk layer prevents bonding. (3) Chalk test — rub white cloth across surface; moderate/heavy chalk = chalk-binding primer required. (4) Moisture probe — moisture meter at siding-to-trim junctions, butt joints, and areas with visible water damage; FC itself doesn't absorb moisture through the face, but water intrusion behind siding at failed joints is detectable. (5) Mildew/algae scan — check north-facing and shaded elevations; common on FC in humid climates. (6) Caulk assessment — 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol on all joints per elevation. Total assessment: ~20-30 min per elevation depending on elevation size and condition.
relevant_findings.source: Exterior_Weathering_Surface_Assessment_Doctrine; SF_SIDING_WOOD_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json (condition assessment pattern); SF_WINDOW_EXT_RP_v1/research.json RF-004 (assessment pattern)

relevant_findings.topic: RRP lead-safe requirements apply to pre-1978 fiber cement siding
relevant_findings.finding: Fiber cement siding was introduced in the 1980s (James Hardie entered US market ~1987), so the VAST MAJORITY of fiber cement siding is post-1978 and does NOT contain lead paint. However, there are edge cases: (1) FC siding installed as replacement on a pre-1978 structure where lead paint from original siding contaminated the substrate area; (2) Very early FC products (pre-1990) that may have been painted with lead-containing primers (rare). The pre-1978 flag is a project-level input — if the BUILDING is pre-1978 even though the siding material is newer, EPA RRP requires testing. In practice, RRP is extremely rare for FC siding RP compared to wood siding RP. Include RRP gate for compliance but note that activation will be uncommon. RRP modifier: 2.0x on prep tasks involving paint disturbance.
relevant_findings.source: EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745; SF_SIDING_WOOD_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json (RRP pattern); SF_TRIM_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json RC-001 (RRP = 2.0x)

relevant_findings.topic: Landscape protection for RP siding includes scraping debris containment
relevant_findings.finding: NC siding landscape protection covers overspray only. RP siding landscape protection also covers: (1) scraping debris (paint chips, potentially lead-containing if RRP applies); (2) rinse water runoff with paint residue; (3) caulk removal debris; (4) sanding dust. Protection scope is larger for RP than NC because scraping and prep generate debris that falls along the entire working elevation. LF-based perimeter protection (same as NC) plus extended landscape coverage when spray application is used. For RRP, protection escalates to 6-mil poly ground containment extending 10 ft from structure per EPA requirements.
relevant_findings.source: Exterior_Protection_Doctrine_T3; SF_SIDING_WOOD_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json (RP protection zones); SF_TRIM_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json (RRP containment pattern)

relevant_findings.topic: End-cut edge sealing is NOT an RP task — already done during NC installation
relevant_findings.finding: NC spec includes TSK_FCSD_SEAL_CUT_EDGES as a mandatory task to prevent edge wicking (FM-001). In RP context, all field-cut edges were sealed during original installation — edge sealing is NOT an RP task. If edge wicking has occurred due to failed sealant, the resulting damage is visible as edge swelling and paint failure at board ends. This is addressed through scraping/feather at the affected area + spot prime with alkali-resistant primer on exposed bare FC at the edge. Edge sealing as a standalone task is NOT_APPLICABLE for RP.

relevant_findings.topic: Condition scale GOOD/FAIR/POOR maps to substrate states and drives prep intensity
relevant_findings.finding: The condition scale provides a simplified 3-tier estimation input that maps to the 4 substrate states: GOOD = SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (minimal prep, degloss/scuff only, no prime needed); FAIR = SS_EXT_CHALKING or localized SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (moderate prep, chalk remediation or moderate scraping, spot or full prime); POOR = SS_EXT_PEELING or widespread SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (heavy prep, extensive scraping/feathering, full prime with alkali-resistant primer on exposed bare FC). Condition modifiers: GOOD=1.0x, FAIR=1.5x, POOR=2.0x. Modifiers apply to prep tasks ONLY — coating application is identical once surface is properly prepared.
relevant_findings.source: controlled_enums.json condition_scale; SF_SIDING_WOOD_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json (condition dimension pattern); SF_WINDOW_EXT_RP_v1/research.json CD-001

relevant_findings.topic: Efflorescence is a fiber-cement-specific RP failure mode not found in wood siding RP
relevant_findings.finding: Efflorescence — white crystalline salt deposits from moisture evaporating through the cementitious matrix — is an FC-specific condition not found on wood siding. In RP context, efflorescence appears as white deposits on or under the existing paint film, often causing blistering or paint lifting. Treatment: dry brush to remove surface deposits, assess moisture source (usually failed flashing or water intrusion behind siding), neutralize with dilute acetic acid (vinegar) if heavy, apply alkali-resistant primer before topcoat. If efflorescence is active (recurring after cleaning), the moisture source must be addressed before painting — otherwise paint will fail again. Efflorescence is an assessment finding, not a substrate state.

relevant_findings.topic: Spray tip selection differs for RP — existing paint film allows different approach
relevant_findings.finding: NC spray tip selection is substrate-driven: 517 for lap/panel, 413 for shingle. RP spray tip selection considers both profile AND existing film condition: sound or chalking surface uses same tips as NC (517 lap/panel, 413 shingle). Failing or peeling surfaces with significant bare areas may benefit from slightly larger tip (519 lap/panel) to increase material deposition for coverage over transition areas between bare FC and existing paint. Backroll pass in RP ensures even coverage regardless of tip size. Spray pressure settings may need adjustment for RP — lower pressure on chalking surfaces to avoid blowing chalk residue.

relevant_findings.topic: Mildew and algae treatment is an RP-specific prep task
relevant_findings.finding: Fiber cement's dense, non-porous surface resists mold penetration but surface mildew and algae growth is common on FC siding in humid climates, especially on north-facing and shaded elevations. In RP, mildew/algae must be treated before painting — painting over mildew causes topcoat failure as organisms continue growing beneath the paint film. Treatment: apply mildewcide solution (dilute bleach or commercial biocide), allow 10-15 min dwell time, rinse with low-pressure water. Follow with standard cleaning. This is an RP-specific task — NC fiber cement does not have mildew/algae because it is freshly installed.

relevant_findings.topic: Customer walkthrough is RP-specific — occupied home context
relevant_findings.finding: RP siding work occurs on occupied homes (unlike NC which is typically unoccupied construction). Customer walkthrough after completion is a standard RP task: walk each elevation with homeowner, verify color/sheen satisfaction, point out any areas of concern, document completion. This is a FIXED task per project (~15-20 min). NC does not include customer walkthrough — the customer is typically the GC or builder, not the homeowner.
relevant_findings.source: SF_SIDING_WOOD_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json (customer walkthrough in scope); SF_WINDOW_EXT_RP_v1/research.json (customer walkthrough RP-new task)

condition_drivers.effect: Primary prep intensity driver. GOOD (SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT): rinse + degloss/scuff only, no prime needed. FAIR (SS_EXT_CHALKING, localized SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT): chalk remediation and/or moderate scraping + spot or full prime. POOR (SS_EXT_PEELING, widespread SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT): heavy scraping/feathering + full prime with alkali-resistant primer on exposed bare FC. Maps to condition_scale: GOOD=1.0x, FAIR=1.5x, POOR=2.0x on prep tasks.
condition_drivers.assessment_method: Visual inspection + ASTM D3359 adhesion test + chalk rub test. Assign per-elevation condition rating.
condition_drivers.source: controlled_enums.json condition_scale; SF_SIDING_WOOD_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json (exterior RP condition pattern)

condition_drivers.effect: Chalking surfaces appear intact but chalk layer prevents topcoat adhesion. Light chalk: low-pressure rinse may remove adequately — test after rinse. Moderate/heavy chalk: chalk-binding primer MANDATORY even after rinse. This is a distinct primer path. FC chalking is the most common RP degradation mode.
condition_drivers.assessment_method: White cloth rub test after low-pressure rinse. Moderate residue = chalk-binding primer required.

condition_drivers.effect: FC siding has extensive caulk joints (siding-to-trim, butt joints, window/door perimeter, foundation transition). Failed caulk = primary water intrusion pathway on FC. Assessment determines scope: intact = clean and paint over; cracked/separated = remove + re-caulk; fully failed = remove all + re-caulk. Rate varies by condition: GOOD = near-zero additional time; FAIR = moderate caulk replacement; POOR = extensive caulk replacement (major labor item).
condition_drivers.assessment_method: 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol per Exterior_Caulking_Sealants_Doctrine. Visual inspection of all joint types per elevation.

condition_drivers.effect: White crystalline salt deposits indicate moisture migrating through or behind the FC substrate. Surface efflorescence: dry brush + neutralize + prime. Active/recurring efflorescence: STOP painting until moisture source is addressed — paint will fail if moisture pathway is not resolved. Efflorescence is FC-specific (cementitious substrate), not found in wood siding RP.
condition_drivers.assessment_method: Visual inspection for white deposits on surface or under paint film. Test for recurrence after cleaning.

condition_drivers.effect: Surface biological growth on FC siding, common on north/shaded elevations in humid climates. Must be treated before painting — organisms continue growing under paint film. Biocide treatment + dwell time + rinse. If heavy, may require second treatment. Assessment finding, not a substrate state — it co-occurs with any state.
condition_drivers.assessment_method: Visual inspection. Green/black discoloration, especially at sheltered areas, under eaves, and north-facing elevations.

condition_drivers.effect: Fiber cement was introduced in the 1980s, so most FC siding is post-1978. RRP is rare for FC siding RP but must be included for compliance when the BUILDING is pre-1978 (siding may have been replaced but building retains lead in other components). Binary gate: pre_1978 + lead-positive = activate RRP. RRP modifier: 2.0x on prep tasks involving paint disturbance. RRP containment setup/teardown are separate fixed tasks per elevation.
condition_drivers.assessment_method: Pre-1978 flag is project-level input. XRF testing or EPA-approved lead test kits if pre-1978.
condition_drivers.source: EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745; SF_TRIM_EXT_RP_v1/spec.json RC-001 (RRP = 2.0x)

condition_drivers.effect: Siding is measured per elevation. Height affects all tasks at elevation: assessment, prep (scraping at height is significantly slower), coating application. ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50. Applied per elevation based on working height. A project may have ground access on one elevation and scaffold on another.
condition_drivers.assessment_method: Per-elevation access assessment during exterior walkthrough. Captured via PS_EXT_META.ENUM.ACCESS_TYPE.

condition_drivers.effect: QT2=economy (single finish coat, minimal inspection). QT3=standard (2 finish coats per Hardie warranty, scan inspection). QT4=premium (2 finish coats, interstage sand, systematic inspection, premium materials). QT5 excluded for siding field per Exterior_Substrates_Doctrine §5.4. QT modifier applies to coating tasks via qt_scaled classification, NOT to prep tasks.

quality_differences.description: Economy exterior FC siding repaint. Rinse, minimal prep (degloss only on sound surfaces), spot prime bare areas only, single finish coat economy-grade 100% acrylic. No interstage sanding. Quick ground-level walkthrough.
quality_differences.inspection: Quick visual at ground level. Note obvious misses.
quality_differences.typical_use: Rental property, pre-sale refresh, budget-constrained. Only appropriate on GOOD condition surfaces.

quality_differences.description: Standard residential FC siding repaint. Full rinse, condition-driven prep, spot or full prime (state-dependent), 2 finish coats mid-grade 100% acrylic (Hardie-approved). Scan inspection at 6-10 ft from ground.
quality_differences.inspection: Ground-level walkthrough at 6-10 ft viewing distance. Check for holidays, runs, overspray on trim.
quality_differences.typical_use: Standard homeowner repaint. Most common residential scenario.

quality_differences.description: Premium FC siding repaint. Full rinse with TSP, thorough condition-driven prep, premium primer, 2 finish coats premium materials (SW Emerald, BM Aura — Hardie-approved). Light sand between finish coats. Systematic inspection at 6 ft.
quality_differences.inspection: Systematic ground-level inspection at 6 ft. With binoculars for upper elevations. All visible defects marked for repair.
quality_differences.typical_use: High-end residential, showcase homes, curb-appeal priority.

failure_modes.cause: Applying topcoat over chalking FC surface without chalk-binding primer. Chalk layer prevents bonding — new paint peels within 1-3 years even with proper application technique.
failure_modes.frequency: Very common on south/west elevations after 8-12 years. Most common RP failure mode for fiber cement.
failure_modes.prevention: Chalk rub test on every elevation. Rinse + chalk-binding primer when chalk is present. Do NOT skip chalk-binding step even if chalk appears light after rinse.
failure_modes.remediation: Full scrape delaminated areas, feather sand, chalk-binding primer, 2 finish coats.

failure_modes.failure: Alkaline burn / saponification at bare FC areas
failure_modes.cause: Applying standard latex primer directly to bare fiber cement (pH 13.0) exposed by scraping. Alkaline environment chemically destroys latex binders. Paint softens, blisters, and detaches.
failure_modes.frequency: Common when inexperienced painters use standard primer on scraped-to-bare FC areas.
failure_modes.prevention: Use alkali-resistant primer (SW Loxon Masonry Primer) on ALL exposed bare FC areas. Never apply standard acrylic latex directly to bare fiber cement.
failure_modes.remediation: Scrape failed coating, clean surface, re-prime with alkali-resistant primer, 2 finish coats.

failure_modes.cause: Painting over active efflorescence without resolving the moisture source. Water continues to migrate through the cementitious matrix, depositing salts that physically push the new paint film off.
failure_modes.frequency: Common when efflorescence is cosmetically cleaned but moisture pathway is not addressed.
failure_modes.prevention: Assess efflorescence for recurrence — clean, wait 48 hr, check for new deposits. If recurring, resolve moisture source (failed flashing, WRB breach, drainage issue) before painting. Alkali-resistant primer over neutralized efflorescence area.
failure_modes.remediation: Resolve moisture source. Remove failed paint. Clean efflorescence deposits. Alkali-resistant primer + 2 finish coats.

failure_modes.failure: Caulk joint failure causing paint failure at board junctions
failure_modes.cause: Failed caulk at siding-to-trim, butt joints, or window/door perimeter allows water behind siding. Moisture-driven paint failure radiates from failed joint outward.
failure_modes.frequency: Very common. Caulk failure is the primary trigger for siding repaint in many cases.
failure_modes.prevention: 'Think Like a Water Drop' caulk assessment at every joint. Replace all failed caulk before painting. Use flexible paintable caulk (polyurethane or siliconized acrylic).
failure_modes.remediation: Remove failed caulk, clean joint, re-caulk, allow cure, scrape/feather affected paint, spot prime, 2 finish coats.

failure_modes.failure: Edge wicking at previously sealed cuts (sealant failure)
failure_modes.cause: Original end-cut edge sealer has failed due to age, UV exposure, or mechanical damage. Water absorbs into exposed cellulose fibers at cut edges, causing edge swelling that ruptures paint film from behind.
failure_modes.frequency: Moderate — edge sealant typically lasts longer than paint film, but can fail at butt joints and window cutouts.
failure_modes.prevention: During RP assessment, inspect board edges at butt joints and openings for swelling. If edge wicking damage is found, scrape affected area, re-seal exposed edge with end-cut sealer or alkali-resistant primer, then prime and coat.
failure_modes.remediation: Scrape to sound substrate, seal exposed edge, alkali-resistant primer on bare FC, 2 finish coats.

failure_modes.failure: Power wash damage to existing paint and substrate texture
failure_modes.cause: Using high-pressure power washer on fiber cement — strips existing paint, damages embossed texture profiles, forces water behind wall assembly.
failure_modes.frequency: Common when inexperienced painters use standard power wash protocol (appropriate for wood) on fiber cement.
failure_modes.prevention: PROHIBIT high-pressure power washing. Use low-pressure rinse only (garden hose + soft brush, or gentle power rinse at 400-600 PSI max). SOP must explicitly state this prohibition.
failure_modes.remediation: Allow wall assembly to fully dry (may take 1-2 weeks if water entered behind siding). Re-assess damage. May require extensive spot prime and recoat.

notes_for_materials_manager.topic: State-driven primer systems for RP fiber cement siding — dual-axis selection
notes_for_materials_manager.note: RP FC siding uses a two-dimensional primer selection: condition state drives primer need, exposed substrate drives primer chemistry. (1) SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT: spot prime bare/thin areas only — standard acrylic exterior primer on areas where existing paint is thin; alkali-resistant primer on any exposed bare FC. No prime needed if no bare areas. (2) SS_EXT_CHALKING: chalk-binding primer full surface (NEW RP system, SYS_FCRP_PRIMER_CHALK_BIND) — applies regardless of underlying substrate. (3) SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT: spot or full prime depending on bare area percentage — alkali-resistant primer on exposed bare FC, acrylic stain-blocking primer on remaining surface. (4) SS_EXT_PEELING: full prime — alkali-resistant primer on all exposed bare FC areas + acrylic stain-blocking over full surface. Key departure from wood siding RP: bare FC requires alkali-resistant primer (pH 13.0), NOT standard acrylic primer.

notes_for_materials_manager.topic: Finish coat systems — same products as NC, adjusted application method
notes_for_materials_manager.note: NC finish systems transfer for product selection: Hardie-approved topcoat systems (SW Duration, SW Emerald, BM Aura or equivalent). QT-driven selection: QT2/QT3 = standard 100% acrylic exterior, QT4 = premium (SW Emerald, BM Aura). Key difference from NC: RP application is spray_backroll (not spray-only) — this does not change the product but may slightly affect coverage rate due to backroll redistribution. Sheens: flat and satin only for siding field.

Add to NC consumable list: (1) chalk-binding primer for SS_EXT_CHALKING; (2) exterior-grade paintable caulk (polyurethane or siliconized acrylic) for caulk replacement; (3) biocide/mildewcide for mildew/algae treatment; (4) alkali-resistant primer (SW Loxon Masonry Primer) for exposed bare FC at peeling/failing areas — this product exists in NC but is triggered by different conditions in RP; (5) RRP containment supplies (6-mil poly, HEPA vacuum, lead-safe disposal bags) when pre_1978 + lead (rare for FC); (6) liquid deglosser or additional sandpaper for existing paint surface preparation.

notes_for_materials_manager.topic: Surface texture affects material quantity — same as NC
notes_for_materials_manager.note: Textured profiles (cedarmill, roughsawn) require 15-30% more material (surface_factor 1.15-1.30 on coverage rate) — identical to NC. This applies to primer and finish coat material quantities. Spray_backroll has slightly lower transfer efficiency than spray-only — factor into material calculation.

notes_for_materials_manager.topic: Caulk quantity is a significant material cost for FC siding RP
notes_for_materials_manager.note: FC siding has more caulk joints than wood siding. Estimate caulk quantity: count LF of all joints requiring re-caulk, plus 15-20% waste for tooling and failed application. Typical 10.3 oz tube covers ~20-25 LF of 1/4" bead. A typical 2500 SF siding repaint may use 8-15 tubes of caulk depending on condition.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: RP fiber cement siding SOP module structure
notes_for_sop_librarian.note: Recommended module structure: (1) MOD_FCRP_ASSESS — assessment module (condition inspect, adhesion test, chalk test, moisture probe, mildew scan, caulk assess per 'Think Like a Water Drop'); (2) MOD_FCRP_PROTECT — protection setup (landscape perimeter, hardscape, fixture masking, HVAC cover, vehicle/driveway + RRP containment if applicable); (3) MOD_FCRP_CLEAN — low-pressure rinse (NOT power wash) + mildew treatment + TSP wash at QT4; (4) MOD_FCRP_PREP — condition-driven prep (scrape/feather failing areas, degloss/scuff sound areas, chalk remediation, efflorescence treatment, dust cleanup); (5) MOD_FCRP_CAULK — caulk assessment and replacement (major scope on FC — separate module due to volume); (6) MOD_FCRP_PRIME — state-driven primer (chalk-binding, spot acrylic, full acrylic, alkali-resistant on bare FC, bonding on ColorPlus substrate); (7) MOD_FCRP_FINISH_1 — finish coat 1 (spray_backroll primary, brush_roll fallback); (8) MOD_FCRP_INTERSTAGE — interstage process (inspect, sand QT4, touch-up, dust); (9) MOD_FCRP_FINISH_2 — finish coat 2 (QT3/QT4); (10) MOD_FCRP_FINAL — final inspection and touchup; (11) MOD_FCRP_CLEANUP — cleanup (protection teardown, equipment clean, site cleanup, customer walkthrough, RRP teardown if applicable).

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: CRITICAL: Low-pressure rinse ONLY — no power washing
notes_for_sop_librarian.note: SOP must EXPLICITLY state that high-pressure power washing is PROHIBITED on fiber cement. Use garden hose + soft bristle brush, or gentle power rinse at 400-600 PSI maximum with 40-60 degree fan tip. This is a departure from wood siding RP and exterior trim RP which allow 1000-1500 PSI power wash. Include prohibition warning in SOP module header.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Caulk module is separate due to high volume on FC siding
notes_for_sop_librarian.note: NC caulk is a single task within the prep module. RP caulk on FC siding deserves its own module (MOD_FCRP_CAULK) because: (1) FC has more caulk joints than wood siding; (2) RP caulk work includes assess + remove + clean + re-caulk + tool for each joint; (3) caulk cure time (2-4 hr) creates a scheduling dependency before painting over joints. Module sequence: assess all joints per elevation → remove failed caulk → clean joints → re-caulk → tool smooth → allow cure.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Spray_backroll is primary RP application — different from NC spray-only
notes_for_sop_librarian.note: NC fiber cement is spray-only (no back-rolling on factory-smooth surface). RP fiber cement uses spray_backroll because the existing painted surface is no longer factory-smooth — weathering, previous coats, repairs, and surface imperfections benefit from backroll to work product into surface for maximum adhesion. This is a 2-person operation: sprayer leads, backroller follows immediately. SOP should specify: spray pass + immediate backroll within wet edge.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Alkali-resistant primer on exposed bare FC — critical RP requirement
notes_for_sop_librarian.note: When scraping exposes bare fiber cement (pH 13.0), alkali-resistant primer is MANDATORY before any other coating. Standard acrylic primer is NOT suitable — will fail via saponification. SOP must flag: after scraping, inspect for exposed bare FC → if bare FC visible → apply alkali-resistant primer (SW Loxon or equivalent) to bare areas → allow cure → then apply standard primer/topcoat to full surface.

notes_for_estimation_engineer.topic: SF-based production with profile and texture modifiers — inherited from NC
notes_for_estimation_engineer.note: This spec uses SF (per siding field area) with siding profile modifier (lap=1.00, panel=1.10, shingle=2.00) and surface texture modifier (smooth=1.00, cedarmill=1.20, roughsawn=1.30). Same PaintScope inputs as NC: IN_SF_SIDING_FIELD, IN_EA_ELEVATIONS, IN_ENUM_ACCESS_TYPE. RP adds: IN_ENUM_SUBSTRATE_STATE, IN_ENUM_SUBSTRATE_CONDITION, IN_BOOL_PRE_1978, IN_LF_CAULK_JOINTS.

notes_for_estimation_engineer.topic: Condition modifiers apply to prep tasks ONLY — stacking partition
notes_for_estimation_engineer.note: Per condition_scale: GOOD=1.0x, FAIR=1.5x, POOR=2.0x. Condition modifier applies to prep tasks only (scrape, feather, sand, chalk remediation, efflorescence treatment, mildew treatment, dust cleanup). NOT applied to protection setup, coating, inspection, or cleanup tasks. Stacking partition follows wood siding RP pattern: prep pool = CONDITION x RRP x ACCESS x PROFILE x TEXTURE; coating pool = QT x ACCESS x PROFILE x TEXTURE. CONDITION and RRP never apply to coating tasks. QT never applies to prep tasks.

notes_for_estimation_engineer.topic: RRP modifier: 2.0x on prep tasks involving paint disturbance — rare for FC
notes_for_estimation_engineer.note: Pre-1978 + lead-positive triggers RRP. FAC_FCRP_RRP = 2.00x on all prep tasks involving paint disturbance (scrape, feather-sand, rinse with paint removal). RRP containment setup/teardown are separate fixed-time tasks per elevation. RRP is very rare for fiber cement siding (FC introduced ~1987) but must be included for EPA compliance when the BUILDING is pre-1978. Binary gate: rrp_required=true or false.

notes_for_estimation_engineer.topic: Spray_backroll production rates — slower than NC spray-only
notes_for_estimation_engineer.note: NC spray-only finish: 300 SF/hr (lap, smooth, ground). RP spray_backroll finish: expect ~225 SF/hr (lap, smooth, ground) — 2-person crew (sprayer + backroller) at similar wall-speed but backroll pass adds ~25% time. This aligns with wood siding spray_backbrush rates. brush_roll fallback: ~80-100 SF/hr (same as NC). Primer spray_backroll rate: ~275-300 SF/hr (vs NC spray-only 350 SF/hr).

notes_for_estimation_engineer.topic: Caulk replacement is a significant line item for FC siding RP
notes_for_estimation_engineer.note: Estimate caulk replacement time: assess + remove + clean + re-caulk + tool at ~60-80 LF/hr for GOOD condition (minimal replacement), ~40-60 LF/hr for FAIR (moderate), ~25-40 LF/hr for POOR (extensive removal + deep cleaning). Caulk LF is a manual capture input — estimator measures total joint length requiring re-caulk per elevation. Typical residential FC siding: 200-500 LF of caulk joints per project.

NC has 25 tasks across 8 modules. RP projection: ~15 DIRECT transfers (protection tasks, finish application, interstage, final inspect/touchup, equipment cleanup, site cleanup) + ~5 MODIFIED (wash becomes low-pressure rinse, scuff sand becomes degloss/scuff, primer becomes state-driven, caulk becomes assess/replace, dust cleanup adds scraping debris) - 2 NOT_APPLICABLE (end-seal cut edges, equipment-setup frequency change) + ~17 RP_NEW (assessment tasks: condition inspect, adhesion test, chalk test, moisture probe, mildew scan, caulk assess; prep tasks: scrape/feather, chalk remediation, efflorescence treatment, mildew treatment, degloss/scuff; caulk tasks: caulk remove/replace; prime tasks: chalk-binding primer, alkali-resistant spot prime; completion: customer walkthrough, RRP containment setup/teardown). Total: approximately 35-40 tasks across 11 modules.

notes_for_estimation_engineer.topic: Modifier stacking partition — prep pool vs coating pool
notes_for_estimation_engineer.note: Prep pool: CONDITION x RRP x ACCESS x PROFILE x TEXTURE. Worst-case prep: POOR (2.0) x RRP (2.0) x scaffold (1.60) x shingle (2.00) x roughsawn (1.30) = 16.64x — extreme edge case, recommend T&M. Common high prep: FAIR (1.5) x no_rrp (1.0) x ladder (1.35) x lap (1.0) x cedarmill (1.20) = 2.43x (within cap). Coating pool: QT x ACCESS x PROFILE x TEXTURE. Worst-case coating: QT4 (1.15) x scaffold (1.60) x shingle (2.00) x roughsawn (1.30) = 4.78x — exceeds 4.0x cap, recommend T&M. Common high coating: QT3 (1.0) x ladder (1.35) x lap (1.0) x cedarmill (1.20) = 1.62x (within cap).

notes_for_estimation_engineer.topic: Environmental conditions are NOT estimation modifiers
notes_for_estimation_engineer.note: Per PaintFactor OS RC-003 and all exterior RP specs: environmental conditions (wind, sun, surface temp, dew point) are NOT estimatable at bid time. They are SOP/scheduling concerns, not production rate modifiers. Excluded from this spec.

notes_for_estimation_engineer.topic: Vehicle/driveway protection zone — RP occupied home
notes_for_estimation_engineer.note: RP siding work occurs on occupied homes. When spray_backroll application is used and vehicles/driveway are adjacent, vehicle/driveway overspray protection is required. This follows the wood siding RP pattern (ext_vehicle_driveway zone). SF-based input.

assumptions.source: Collision analysis against all NC and RP specs
assumptions.note: TSK_FCSD_* is consumed by NC (25 tasks). FCRP_ avoids all collisions. Pattern: FC = fiber cement, RP = repaint.

assumptions.value: spray_backroll is primary RP method (departure from NC spray-only)
assumptions.note: NC FC is spray-only (factory-smooth surface). RP FC uses spray_backroll because existing painted surface benefits from backroll for adhesion. Doctrine guidance: 'Back-rolling introduces unwanted stipple/orange peel' applies to factory-smooth FC only — RP surface is no longer factory-smooth.

assumptions.value: 4 exterior RP states: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT, SS_EXT_CHALKING, SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT, SS_EXT_PEELING
assumptions.note: Standard 4-state exterior RP pattern. SS_EXT_WEATHERED excluded — bare FC with no coating is NC territory. SS_EXT_STAINED_* excluded.

assumptions.value: GOOD=1.0x, FAIR=1.5x, POOR=2.0x on prep tasks only
assumptions.note: Standard exterior RP condition modifier pattern. Maps to substrate states per RF-013.
NC uses 4-tier access per elevation. Transfers unchanged to RP. Modifier values: ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50.

assumptions.value: FAC_FCRP_RRP = 2.00x on prep tasks involving paint disturbance
assumptions.note: RRP modifier calibrated to 2.0x per established exterior RP pattern. Consistent across all exterior RP specs.

assumptions.value: NC finish application, interstage, final inspect/touchup, and cleanup rates transfer with adjustment for spray_backroll vs spray-only
assumptions.note: Once surface is properly prepped and primed, coating application is similar. spray_backroll is ~25% slower than spray-only due to backroll pass. Protection and cleanup rates transfer unchanged.
QT5 reserved for fine exterior millwork, not siding field. Same as NC.

assumptions.value: flat, satin (NOT semi-gloss or gloss — siding uses lower sheens)
assumptions.note: Siding field uses flat or satin. Semi-gloss/gloss reserved for trim and fine-finish surfaces.

uncertainties.topic: spray_backroll vs spray-only for RP fiber cement
uncertainties.description: The NC spec explicitly prohibits back-rolling on fiber cement (factory-smooth surface produces stipple). The RP context has an existing paint film that is no longer factory-smooth. Should RP use spray_backroll (for adhesion into surface imperfections) or maintain spray-only (preserve smooth appearance)? Research recommends spray_backroll based on wood siding RP pattern and practical adhesion considerations, but this is a departure from NC doctrine.
uncertainties.impact: Application method drives production rate, crew size, and defect tolerance
uncertainties.resolution: Recommend spray_backroll as primary for v1 with spray-only as optional for sound-condition surfaces where the existing film is smooth. Flag for Eric review.

uncertainties.topic: Condition modifier values for FC-specific prep tasks
uncertainties.description: The GOOD/FAIR/POOR condition modifiers (1.0x/1.5x/2.0x) are inherited from the general exterior RP pattern. FC-specific prep tasks (efflorescence treatment, chalk remediation on dense cementitious surface) may have different labor intensity than the general pattern suggests. Chalk remediation on FC may be easier than on wood (FC is non-porous, chalk sits on surface) or harder (dense surface resists primer penetration).
uncertainties.resolution: Use standard condition modifiers for v1. Flag efflorescence and chalk tasks for field calibration.

uncertainties.topic: Caulk replacement labor as standalone module vs integrated prep task
uncertainties.description: FC siding has significantly more caulk joints than wood siding. Should caulk assessment/replacement be a standalone module (MOD_FCRP_CAULK) or remain integrated within the prep module? Standalone module provides better labor tracking and scheduling (caulk cure time is a dependency). Integrated approach is simpler.
uncertainties.impact: Module structure, scheduling accuracy, and labor tracking
uncertainties.resolution: Recommend standalone module for v1 due to high caulk volume and cure-time scheduling dependency.

uncertainties.topic: Rinse/cleaning ownership overlap with other exterior RP specs
uncertainties.description: Low-pressure rinse covers an entire elevation — siding, trim, windows are all rinsed in one pass. If multiple exterior RP specs are active on the same elevation, rinse should not be double-counted. Same concern as power wash ownership in SF_WINDOW_EXT_RP_v1 U-003.
uncertainties.resolution: Recommend rinse owned by the spec that initiates the exterior RP sequence on each elevation. Cross-spec deduplication rule: if rinse/wash is already performed by another spec on the same elevation, skip. Flag for Estimation Engineer.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray_backroll
zones.notes: LF-based — measured along house perimeter where landscape is adjacent. brush_roll: drop cloth at base. spray_backroll: full tarp width over plantings. RP adds: scraping debris containment (paint chips fall along working elevation). RRP: further upgrades to 6-mil poly via ext_rrp_containment zone.
RP-SPECIFIC: extended overspray zone beyond perimeter. Spray only. Follows wood siding RP pattern.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray_backroll
zones.notes: Walkways adjacent to siding. Canvas drop cloths for non-slip crew traffic. RP adds: scraping debris protection.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray_backroll
zones.notes: Patio adjacent to siding. Protection level driven by proximity and application method.
All exterior fixtures on working elevations. Bag or tape over fixture. Same as NC.
HVAC condenser units adjacent to siding. Full tarp cover during spray operations. Same as NC.
RP-SPECIFIC: occupied home. Vehicles and driveway surface require overspray protection during spray application. Follows wood siding RP pattern.

EPA RRP Rule (40 CFR 745). 6-mil poly ground containment extending 10 ft from structure. Required when disturbing lead paint on pre-1978 structures. Per-elevation setup. Rare for FC siding but included for compliance.

protection_zones_analysis.cross_spec_protection_note: Window and door protection during siding work is NOT this spec's responsibility. Window/door masking belongs in the respective window or door spec. Landscape/hardscape protection may overlap with trim and window RP specs when multiple exterior specs are active — deduplication rule applies.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Soffit at eave. Often different color. Separate scope. RP: soffit is almost always already painted — light masking at siding-soffit junction during spray.
Frieze board at siding-to-soffit junction. Trim color. Separate scope (SF_TRIM_EXT_RP). RP: caulk at siding-to-frieze junction is THIS spec's responsibility.
Corner boards frame siding. Trim color. Separate scope. RP: caulk at siding-to-corner junction is THIS spec's responsibility.
Window casing. Siding terminates at casing. Window/door protection is window/door spec's responsibility. RP: caulk at siding-to-casing junction is THIS spec's responsibility.
Door casing. Same as window casing relationship. RP: caulk at siding-to-casing junction is THIS spec's responsibility.
Foundation below siding. Not painted in siding scope. Drop cloth protection at grade level handled by landscape/hardscape protection zones.

adjacency_analysis.key_finding: Identical adjacency pattern to NC siding. Siding field has NO edge work requirements. All adjacent surfaces are separate specs (soffit, trim, foundation) or not in scope. Protection and caulk relationships only. RP adds caulk assessment/replacement responsibility at ALL siding-to-trim junctions.

affected_conditions.notes: HEIGHT IS A MAJOR MODIFIER for siding. Applied to ALL per-elevation tasks at height. Per-elevation attribute via PS_EXT_META.ENUM.ACCESS_TYPE. Follows NC 4-tier model. Protection setup/teardown and fixed assessment tasks are NOT affected.

Condition modifier applies to prep tasks ONLY. Maps from substrate state: GOOD=SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT, FAIR=SS_EXT_CHALKING or localized SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT, POOR=SS_EXT_PEELING or widespread SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT.
Pre-1978 + lead-positive triggers RRP. 2.0x on prep tasks involving paint disturbance. Binary gate. Rare for FC siding. RRP containment setup/teardown are separate fixed tasks per elevation.

affected_conditions.modifier_notes: Triggers lead assessment and potential RRP activation
affected_conditions.notes: Project-level flag. FC siding was introduced ~1987 so most FC is post-1978, but building structure may be pre-1978 with replacement siding.

excluded_conditions.reason: Environmental conditions are NOT estimation modifiers per PaintFactor OS RC-003. Wind affects scheduling, not production rate estimation.
Environmental conditions are NOT estimation modifiers per PaintFactor OS RC-003.
Environmental conditions are NOT estimation modifiers per PaintFactor OS RC-003.
Environmental conditions are NOT estimation modifiers per PaintFactor OS RC-003.

valid_input_states.rationale: 4 exterior RP substrate states — standard for all exterior RP specs. SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT is most common for well-maintained FC (cosmetic refresh). SS_EXT_CHALKING is the most common degradation state for FC (UV-driven binder breakdown on dense cementitious substrate). SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT = cracking at stress points (joints, corners). SS_EXT_PEELING = active delamination, often at caulk failure points or moisture intrusion areas. SS_EXT_WEATHERED excluded (bare FC territory = NC). SS_EXT_STAINED_* excluded. Per-elevation substrate state if conditions differ.

output_state.rationale: All repaint input states converge to painted output state. Satin is the most common exterior siding sheen. Flat available for economy applications.

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: In RP, trim is almost always already painted. Mask to prevent overspray on finished trim. Spray_backroll requires full masking of adjacent trim.
In RP, soffit is almost always already finished. Light masking at siding-soffit junction. Spray drift is primarily downward/lateral — soffit is overhead and receives less exposure.
Foundation wall is rarely painted. Drop cloth at grade level is handled by landscape/hardscape protection zones.

modified_transfers.rationale: NC low-pressure wash removes construction dust; RP low-pressure rinse removes weathering dirt, chalk residue, mildew — same method (garden hose, NO power washing) but different purpose and may require TSP at QT4. Rate similar but RP includes pre-rinse surface assessment.
NC scuffs factory primer for adhesion profile; RP degloss/scuffs existing paint for topcoat adhesion. Different substrate (existing paint vs factory primer) but similar technique.
NC applies fresh caulk at siding-to-trim joints; RP assesses ALL joints + removes failed caulk + re-caulks. Significantly higher scope — assess + remove + clean + apply vs apply only.
NC removes sanding dust; RP removes sanding dust + scraping debris + chalk residue. Slightly more volume.
NC spray-only primer; RP spray_backroll primer (existing surface benefits from backroll for adhesion). 2-person crew. ~25% slower than spray-only.
Same method (brush/roll) but RP primer is state-driven (chalk-binding, acrylic, or alkali-resistant) rather than substrate-driven.
NC spray-only finish; RP spray_backroll finish. 2-person crew. ~25% slower.
NC spray-only finish coat 2; RP spray_backroll. Same modification as finish coat 1.
RP setup includes backroll equipment staging (roller covers, trays) in addition to spray setup. Slightly longer (~50 min vs 45 min).

not_applicable.rationale: End-cut edge sealing was performed during NC installation. Not an RP task. Edge wicking damage in RP is addressed via scrape + spot prime.

rp_new_tasks: TSK_FCRP_ASSESS_CONDITION — visual condition inspection of all siding surfaces per elevation, DSD-equivalent rating, photograph defects, assign substrate state
TSK_FCRP_ASSESS_ADHESION — ASTM D3359 cross-hatch tape test on representative sections per elevation
TSK_FCRP_ASSESS_CHALK — white cloth chalk rub test per elevation (exterior-specific)
TSK_FCRP_ASSESS_MOISTURE — moisture meter probe at siding-to-trim junctions, butt joints, water damage areas
TSK_FCRP_ASSESS_MILDEW — scan for mildew/algae presence, especially north/shaded elevations
TSK_FCRP_ASSESS_CAULK — caulk assessment per 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol, all joint types per elevation
TSK_FCRP_MILDEW_TREAT — biocide/mildewcide application + dwell time + rinse for mildew/algae
TSK_FCRP_SCRAPE_FEATHER — scrape failing/peeling paint + feather-edge sand all scraped areas (condition-gated: FAIR/POOR only)
TSK_FCRP_CHALK_REMEDIATION — chalk-binding primer application for SS_EXT_CHALKING surfaces
TSK_FCRP_EFFLORESCENCE_TREAT — dry brush + neutralize efflorescence deposits (FC-specific)
TSK_FCRP_CAULK_REMOVE — remove failed caulk from joints (separate from replacement for rate tracking)
TSK_FCRP_CAULK_REPLACE — re-caulk cleaned joints with exterior-grade paintable caulk + tool smooth
TSK_FCRP_PRIME_SPOT_ALKALI — alkali-resistant primer spot application on exposed bare FC areas (SW Loxon or equivalent)
TSK_FCRP_PRIME_CHALK_BIND — chalk-binding primer full surface application for SS_EXT_CHALKING
TSK_FCRP_LANDSCAPE_FULL_PROTECT — extended landscape overspray protection (spray_backroll, RP-specific)
TSK_FCRP_VEHICLE_PROTECT — vehicle/driveway overspray protection (occupied home, spray_backroll)
TSK_FCRP_RRP_CONTAINMENT_SETUP — EPA RRP containment setup per elevation (pre-1978 + lead, rare for FC)
TSK_FCRP_RRP_CONTAINMENT_TEARDOWN — EPA RRP containment teardown and lead-safe disposal
TSK_FCRP_CUSTOMER_WALKTHROUGH — post-completion review with homeowner (verify color, sheen, coverage per elevation)

change_log.author: Spec Researcher Agent
change_log.changes: Initial research.json for SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_RP_v1. Derived from SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_NC_v1 (25 tasks) as primary template, with exterior RP patterns from SF_SIDING_WOOD_EXT_RP_v1, SF_TRIM_EXT_RP_v1, and SF_WINDOW_EXT_RP_v1. Context prefix FCRP_ avoids collision with TSK_FCSD_* NC tasks. 4 exterior RP substrate states (SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT, SS_EXT_CHALKING, SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT, SS_EXT_PEELING). Key FC-specific RP findings: (1) spray_backroll replaces spray-only as primary method (RF-001 — existing painted surface is no longer factory-smooth, benefits from backroll for adhesion); (2) NO power washing even for RP — low-pressure rinse only (RF-002); (3) chalking is the dominant degradation mode for FC (RF-005); (4) exposed bare FC from scraping requires alkali-resistant primer at pH 13.0 (RF-004); (5) caulk assessment/replacement is MAJOR scope (RF-006); (6) efflorescence is FC-specific failure mode (RF-014); (7) RRP is rare for FC siding (introduced ~1987) but included for compliance (RF-010). Projected 42 tasks: 12 DIRECT transfers + 12 MODIFIED - 1 NOT_APPLICABLE (end-seal) + 19 RP_NEW (6 assessment, mildew treat, scrape/feather, chalk remediation, efflorescence treat, caulk remove/replace, alkali-resistant spot prime, chalk-binding prime, extended landscape/vehicle protection, RRP containment, customer walkthrough). NC modifiers (profile lap/panel/shingle, texture smooth/cedarmill/roughsawn, access ground/ladder/scaffold/lift) transfer unchanged. RP adds condition modifiers (GOOD/FAIR/POOR) on prep tasks and RRP modifier (2.0x) on prep tasks (rare activation). Stacking partition: prep pool = CONDITION x RRP x ACCESS x PROFILE x TEXTURE; coating pool = QT x ACCESS x PROFILE x TEXTURE. QT2-QT4 (QT5 excluded for siding field). Sheens: flat, satin. 8 protection zones (5 from NC + 3 RP-new: landscape_full, vehicle_driveway, rrp_containment). 6 failure modes. 8 condition drivers. 11 modules recommended.
